rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is the foremost practical manifestation of the submission to God commanded in the preceding verse.
rows.anchor: The prayer has been mentioned here as the foremost practical manifestation of the Islam mentioned earlier

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to submit includes abiding by all limits God has commanded.
rows.anchor: The word here refers to abiding by all those limits that God has commanded to abide by.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being gathered to God refers to the Hereafter and God's oneness; this supports prayer and obedience because all will appear before God alone, with no other protector.
rows.anchor: The expression “towards Him shall all of you be gathered” refers to both the hereafter and to the oneness of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that God created the heavens and earth in truth concisely argues for every aspect of the gathering before Him.
rows.anchor: the verse “and it is He alone Who has created the heavens and the earth in all truth” is a very comprehensive one

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs of God's power, wisdom, mercy, and providence show that the world is purposeful rather than amusement, so it must culminate in justice that rewards virtue and punishes vice.
rows.anchor: The signs and arguments present in the heavens and the earth regarding the Creator’s power, wisdom and providence bear witness

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without a final judgment, good and evil and justice and injustice would be equal in God's sight, which human nature cannot accept; therefore a day of justice must come.
rows.anchor: If it continues like this, the oppression in it is not redeemed through a day of justice, fairness is not rewarded

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's word certainly brings the Day of Judgment with one utterance; creating the world once posed no difficulty, so recreating it will not either.
rows.anchor: The words “His word is certain to materialize” mean that none should have any doubt

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God is wise and knowledgeable, His judgments rest on justice, wisdom, and knowledge, with no defect that could invert truth and falsehood or cause error.
rows.anchor: God is wise as well as knowledgeable. For this reason, the essential consequence of this is that all His verdicts be based on justice, wisdom and knowledge.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coming passage refutes idolater innovations claimed as Abrahamic inheritance, identifying them as Satan's inspirations and baseless prohibitions of lawful things.
rows.anchor: the religious innovations of Idolaters are refuted. They claimed that these innovations were inherited by them from Abraham (sws) whereas actually they were Satan’s inspirations.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idolaters claimed that the Prophet permitted what their ancestors had forbidden since Abraham and Ishmael; this propaganda readily affected people of weak temperament.
rows.anchor: they raised the propaganda that Mu ḥammad (sws) had allowed things their ancestors had forbidden ever since the times of Abraham (sws) and Ishmael (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eating and drinking are sensitive matters, especially when tied to idolatrous innovations, so the Qur'an refutes these claims in detail and explains Abraham's true way.
rows.anchor: human dispositions are very sensitive in the matters of eating and drinking, and if these matters relate to idolatrous innovations, their impact is very swift.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subject continues to the sūrah's end, with intervening discussions serving as comments or refutations that directly or indirectly relate to it.
rows.anchor: This subject will now continue until the end of the sūrah. In between, certain things are also discussed as on the spot of comments or refutation of doubts.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolaters' campaign arose because the Qur'an declared lawful animals they had prohibited through polytheistic superstition.
rows.anchor: when the Qur’ ān regarded those animals as lawful for eating which the idolaters had prohibited because of their polytheistic superstitions

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They argued that the Prophet permitted what their ancestors had forbidden since Abraham and Ishmael.
rows.anchor: They contended that the Prophet (sws) was regarding as lawful what had been regarded as unlawful ever since the time of their ancestors Abraham (sws) and Ishmael (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says people generally have weak faith and heightened sensitivity in such matters.
rows.anchor: the general mind is prone to weak faith and is also very sensitive.
